title_en: Solutions (fragment from a treatise on the solution of dogmatic questions)
author: Cyril of Alexandria
addressee: a pious reader addressed as 'your reverence'
occasion: The fragment answers objections or questions about biblical narratives, especially whether the rich man and Lazarus account describes events that actually happened and how to understand the prophet Hosea's marriage and Melchizedek's origin.
argument: The fragment opens with the gospel story of the rich man and Lazarus and their opposite fates after death. An unnamed interlocutor then poses the question whether this story already happened and each received due recompense, or whether it typifies the coming judgment; the interlocutor argues that because Jesus names Lazarus, the account is true and was really enacted. Cyril's own response is only partially preserved in the lacunose heading 'Solution: the judgment...' that follows. The fragment then raises further questions about whether Hosea really married a prostitute and had children by her in actual deed, or whether these things are said prophetically, and about whether Melchizedek was an ordinary man, a spirit, or a man newly created by God without human origin. Cyril refers the reader to his fuller discussions in his commentary on Hosea and in his work on Genesis.

outline.move: The fragment opens by summarizing the gospel story of the rich man and Lazarus and their opposite fates after death.

An interlocutor poses the question whether this story already happened and each received due recompense, or whether it typifies the coming judgment, and argues that the naming of Lazarus shows it truly happened; Cyril's own response is only partially preserved in the lacunose heading that follows.
The fragment raises further questions about whether Hosea really married a prostitute and had children by her, and about the nature and origin of Melchizedek.
Cyril refers the reader to his fuller treatment of these topics in his writings on Hosea and on Genesis.

cast.name: Lazarus
cast.who: The poor man in the gospel story, covered with sores and laid at the rich man's gate.

cast.name: Hosea
cast.who: The Old Testament prophet whose marriage to a prostitute is discussed.

cast.name: Melchizedek
cast.who: The biblical priest-king whose origin and nature are questioned.

voices.speaker: an unnamed interlocutor or objector
voices.how_marked: introduced by 'he says' (φησίν); the interlocutor argues that the naming of Lazarus proves the story really happened, a position Cyril then engages with

key_terms.sense: The punishment or retribution the rich man undergoes after death.
The rest or repose the poor man Lazarus enters after death.
The due recompense or repayment each person receives according to his deeds.
The future judgment of which the Lazarus story may be an image or type.
The image or figure by which the story may represent the coming judgment.
The naming or appellation of Lazarus, used by the interlocutor as evidence that the account is historical.
The prostitute whom Hosea was commanded to take as wife.
The manner in which prophetic actions or words may be understood symbolically rather than literally.
The beginning or origin of Melchizedek's coming into being, which the fragment says was not from human parents.
candidates: origin of his coming into being

key_terms.sense: Melchizedek's being created directly by God, recently, rather than born from humans.

scripture: The fragment refers to the gospel story of the rich man and Lazarus, the prophet Hosea, and Melchizedek from Genesis. The author's fuller discussions are said to be found in his commentary on Hosea and in his book on Genesis. Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and numbering.
uncertain: The exact date of the work is not stated in the fragment.
The precise identity of the addressee beyond 'your reverence' is not given.
The full original scope and structure of the treatise cannot be reconstructed from this fragment.
Cyril's own position on the Lazarus question is only partially preserved in the lacunose heading 'Ἐπίλυσις Τὴν κρίσιν κτλ.'

_unresolved_facts.claim: especially whether the rich man and Lazarus account describes events that actually happened
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ταῦτα ἤδη γέγονε καὶ ἀνταπόδοσις ἀξία ἐκληρώθη ἑκάστῳ, ἢ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως ἀνατυποῖ τὴν εἰκόνα ἐν τούτοις;
_unresolved_facts.fix: The interlocutor asks whether the story already happened and each received due recompense, OR whether it typifies the coming judgment—presenting two alternatives, not simply asking whether it 'actually happened'

_unresolved_facts.claim: An unnamed interlocutor then poses the question whether this story already happened and each received due recompense, or whether it typifies the coming judgment
_unresolved_facts.fix: The interlocutor poses the question but the 'or' alternative (typifying the coming judgment) is the other option the interlocutor presents; the brief should clarify that the interlocutor argues FOR the 'already happened' view, not merely poses it as a neutral question

_unresolved_facts.claim: the interlocutor argues that because Jesus names Lazarus, the account is true and was really enacted
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁπότε ὀνομάζει Λαζάρου προσηγορίαν, ἀληθῶς γέγονε καὶ ἐπράχθη
_unresolved_facts.fix: the interlocutor argues that because HE (the evangelist/Jesus) NAMES Lazarus with a proper name, this shows it truly happened and was enacted in experience and truth (πείρᾳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ)

_unresolved_facts.claim: Cyril's own response is only partially preserved in the lacunose heading 'Solution: the judgment...' that follows
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyril's response begins with 'Ἐπίλυσις Τὴν κρίσιν κτλ.'—the heading marks the start of his solution, but we cannot confirm it is 'lacunose' from this fragment; it may simply be abbreviated in the manuscript

_unresolved_facts.claim: whether Hosea really married a prostitute and had children by her in actual deed, or whether these things are said prophetically
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Εἰ ἔλαβεν Ὠσηὲ ὁ προφήτης γυναῖκα πόρνην καὶ ἐτέκνωσεν ἐξ αὐτῆς πράξει καὶ ἐνεργείᾳ, ἢ προφητικῶς νοούμενα λέγει
_unresolved_facts.fix: whether Hosea the prophet took a wife, a prostitute, and had children by her in deed and actuality, or whether being understood prophetically he speaks

_unresolved_facts.claim: about whether Melchizedek was an ordinary man, a spirit, or a man newly created by God without human origin
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Εἰ ὁ Μελχισεδὲκ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος ἁπλῶς οὐδὲ πνεῦμα, ἀλλ' ἄνθρωπος ἀρχὴν γενέσεως οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἔχων ἀλλὰ προσφάτως δημιουργηθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: about whether Melchizedek was not simply a man nor a spirit, but a man not having the beginning of his birth from humans but recently/newly created by God

_unresolved_facts.claim: introduced by 'he says' (φησίν); the interlocutor argues that the naming of Lazarus proves the story really happened, a position Cyril then engages with
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἀλλά, φησίν, ὁπότε ὀνομάζει Λαζάρου προσηγορίαν, ἀληθῶς γέγονε καὶ ἐπράχθη
_unresolved_facts.fix: introduced by 'but, he says' (ἀλλά, φησίν); the interlocutor argues that the naming of Lazarus proves the story truly happened and was enacted, a position Cyril then answers with his 'Solution'
